fatal_errors: The proposed Al0.5NbTa0.8Ti1.5V0.2Zr refractory HEA is not the target AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA.

The hypothesis conflates aging temperature with mechanical-test temperature. The target transition arises among specimens aged within a 550–750 °C window and subsequently tested, whereas the proposal predicts a transition during testing at different temperatures.
Evidence E1 supports microstructural inversion and improved room-temperature compressive ductility, but it does not establish a ductility minimum near 600 °C followed by recovery above 600 °C.

The proposed BCC/B2 precipitation-strengthening and slip-system activation mechanism omits the target L12 ordering, elevated APBE, planar slip, jagged FCC/B2 phase boundaries, and ductile phase-boundary transition zones.
The claimed high-temperature recovery is speculative because the cited study reports tests only at 25 °C and 600 °C, not the proposed 800 °C recovery condition.
explanation: The response addresses the general idea of a ductile–brittle–ductile response in a compositionally complex alloy, but reconstructs a different material, treatment, and mechanism. Its cited evidence credibly supports an inverted BCC/B2 microstructure and improved room-temperature ductility in the refractory HEA, not the asserted non-monotonic temperature dependence. The falsification experiment is reasonably discriminating because it directly measures ductility at three temperatures and verifies the microstructure, but it would test a new speculative alternative rather than reproduce the reported aging-induced transition. The target is AlCoCrFeNi2.1 aged near 600 °C and 750 °C, with embrittlement controlled by enhanced L12 ordering and jagged FCC/B2 boundaries and recovery associated with reduced ordering and ductile boundary zones.
